segments.text:
Verſ. 21.
To goe into the holes of the rocks, and into the tops of the ragged rocks, from before the feare of the Lord, and from the glorie of his maieſtie, when he ſhall riſe to deſtroy the earth.

THis is no ſuperfluous repetitiō, although Iſaiah repeates the ſame things whereof hee ſpake but erewhile. For is there any thing more difficult then to pricke, & wound men to the quicke, and to prouoke them to the true feare of God? We perceiue this, not onely in hypocrits, but euen in our ſelues, if we looke narrowly into it. For how many
things are ſet before vs, by which our minds ought to bee rauiſhed; and yet notwithſtanding wee are ſcarce once mooued therewith? It was chiefly neceſſary that this iudgement of God ſhould be repeated to the hypocrits, who pleaſed themſelues in their wickednes. Now the ſeueritie of Gods vengeance is therein manifeſted, namely, that the wicked choſe rather to be ſwallowed vp into the deepeſt gulfes that may be, then to come neere into his ſight. From this place it ſeemes that Chriſt borrowed that wherewith he threatens the Iewes; in that day they ſhall ſay to the mountaines couer vs, and to the hills, hide vs. Luk. 23.30.
